chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'When the time for the obligatory prayer enters, should I pray the optional prayer or begin with the obligatory prayer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'The preference is that you begin with the obligatory prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Should I pray optional prayers before or after the obligatory prayer when times overlap?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of prayers when their times overlap, establishing that while optional prayers are virtuous, the obligatory prayer takes precedence to ensure its timely fulfillment. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of 'priority of the obligatory' (tarjih al-fard), preventing the neglect of the primary duty due to the pursuit of supererogatory acts. It serves as a practical guideline for believers to maintain the integrity of the five daily prayers amidst voluntary devotion.
